name: plex-dbrepair
description: Plex DBRepair is a one shot Plex database maintenance tool using ChuckPa DBRepair version 26 10 00 Automatically discovers a running Plex Docker container through the host Docker socket and copies the DBRepair executable into it Stops the Plex Media Server process while keeping the Docker container running where supported Performs the selected database maintenance operation and restarts the Plex container after success No Plex appdata mount is required in the repair container Supported modes are automatic check vacuum repair reindex deflate and prune If more than one Plex container is detected set PLEX_CONTAINER_NAME to the exact container name Persistent logs are stored in the logs directory Database backups are enabled by default for all modes except prune CAUTION This tool modifies Plex databases and users are responsible for maintaining verified backups Tested successfully with LinuxServer Plex on a disposable installation Binhex and Hotio compatibility has not yet been verified If the Plex process restarts unexpectedly or the Plex container exits during maintenance the repair operation may stop without restarting Plex Set the repair container restart policy to No to prevent repeated maintenance operations

paths.name: Persistent Repair Logs
paths.description: Host folder for timestamped DBRepair execution logs. Docker logs also show output.

paths.name: Host Docker Socket
paths.description: REQUIRED: Docker host socket for discovering Plex and running docker inspect/exec/cp/restart. Grants this tool host-level Docker control.

variables.name: Maintenance Mode
variables.description: automatic=upstream auto; check=integrity checks; vacuum=compact; repair=rebuild including FTS; reindex=rebuild indexes; deflate=compact only if needed; prune=PhotoTranscoder cleanup. Select one mode.

variables.name: Plex Container Name
variables.description: auto detects one eligible Plex container. If you have multiple Plex containers, enter the exact Docker container name shown by docker ps (example: plex). Do not enter a Docker image name here.

variables.name: Enable Database Backups
variables.description: Create timestamped cold database archives inside the TARGET Plex container at Plex Media Server/DBRepair-Backups; skipped for prune. Backups take disk space and are not automatically deleted.

variables.name: Restart Plex After Success
variables.description: Restart the target Plex Docker container after successful maintenance. On database errors the script intentionally does not auto-restart Plex.

variables.name: Prune Days
variables.description: For prune mode only: remove eligible PhotoTranscoder cached files older than this number of days.

variables.name: Plex Container Match
variables.description: Case-insensitive name substring used when Plex Container Name=auto. Image names containing plex are also considered. Candidates must contain the Plex database at the configured path.

variables.name: Plex Internal Config Mount
variables.description: Path INSIDE the target Plex container to its config mount, usually /config. This is NOT a host volume to mount to DBRepair.

variables.name: Plex Internal Relative Path
variables.description: Relative path inside the target Plex container's config directory. Leave at default unless that Plex installation differs.

variables.name: Allow Process Shutdown Fallback
variables.description: If upstream DBRepair stop cannot shut down Plex, allow SIGTERM to the Plex Media Server process. No forced Docker stop/offline repair fallback is implemented.

variables.name: Maintenance Timeout Seconds
variables.description: Maximum DBRepair operation duration in seconds. A failure or timeout requires reviewing the database before restarting Plex.

variables.name: Plex Shutdown Timeout Seconds
variables.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the Plex process to stop before aborting.
